translation.text: I began to speak the third parable, concerning the righteous and the chosen.[a]

footnotes.text: The selected text explicitly introduces the third parable, concerning both the righteous and the chosen. Neither the ordinal nor either group is omitted.

source.text: *ብፁዓን፡ እንትሙ፡ ጻድቃን፡ ወኅሩያን፡ እስመ፡ ስቡሕ፡ ክፍልክሙ።

translation.text: Blessed are you, righteous and chosen ones, for your portion is glorious.[a]

footnotes.text: The address is directly to you, righteous and chosen ones. Glorious retains the source adjective for their portion rather than silently changing the statement into a prediction.

source.text: ወይከውኑ፡ ጻድቃን፡ *በብርሃነ፡ ፀሐይ፡ ወኅሩያን፡ በብርሃነ፡ ሕይወት፡ ዘለዓለም፡ ወማኅለቅት፡ አልቦት፡ መዋዕለ፡ ሕይወቶሙ፡ ወቅዱሳን፡ ኁልቆ፡ መዋዕል፡ አልቦሙ።
source.note: Actual Charles1906 complete-unit full-page and native400dpi visual collation. Printed editorial readings remain selected print, not independent manuscript certification. No reported variant outside this main-text base adopted. Independent exact-row review required.

translation.text: The righteous will be in the light of the sun, and the chosen in the light of everlasting life. Their days of life have no end, and the holy ones have no count of days.[a]

footnotes.text: The selected text distinguishes light of the sun from light of everlasting life. It then denies an end to their days of life and a count of days to the holy ones. The last holy-ones clause is retained rather than clipped or folded into the previous noun.

source.text: ወይኀሥሥዎ፡ ለብርሃን፡ ወ*ይረክቡ፡ ጽድቀ፡ በኀበ፡ እግዚአ፡ መንፈሳት፡ ሰላም፡ ለጻድቃን፡ በስመ፡ እግዚአ፡ ዓለም።

translation.text: They will seek the light and find righteousness with the Lord of Spirits. Peace to the righteous in the name of the Lord of the world![a]

footnotes.text: The first clause seeks light but finds righteousness; these are not silently made the same noun. The closing title is Lord of the world, whereas the preceding title is Lord of Spirits.

source.text: ወእምድኅረዝ፡ ይትበሀል፡ ለቅዱሳን፡ በሰማይ፡ ከመ፡ ይትኀሥሡ፡ ኅቡአተ፡ ጽድቅ፡ ክፍለ፡ ኀይማኖት፡ እስመ፡ ሠረቀ፡ ከመ፡ ፀሐይ፡ ዲበ፡ *የብስ፡ ወ*ጽልመት፡ ኀለፈት።

translation.text: After this the holy ones in heaven will be told to seek the hidden things of righteousness, the portion of faith, for it has risen like the sun upon dry land, and darkness has passed away.[a]

footnotes.text: The whole unit continues onto the next page. Portion of faith preserves the selected words without adding a lottery or a previously unmentioned recipient. The selected rising clause has an unnamed singular subject, rendered it in English; this unit does not print a light noun or securely identify that antecedent. It has risen like the sun upon dry land, and darkness has passed away.

source.text: ወብርሃን፡ ዘኢ*ይትኄለቍ፡ ይከውን፡ ወበኁልቍ፡ መዋዕል፡ ኢይትወሰን፡ እስመ፡ ቀዳሚ፡ ተኀትተት፡ ጽልመት፡ ወብርሃን፡ ትጸንዕ፡ በቅድመ፡ እግዚአ፡ መንፈሳት፡ ወብርሃን፡ ርትዕ፡ ትጸንዕ፡ ለዓለም፡ በቅድመ፡ እግዚአ፡ መንፈሳት።

translation.text: There will be light that cannot be counted, and it will not be bounded by a number of days. For darkness was first examined, and light will stand firm before the Lord of Spirits. Upright light will stand firm for ever before the Lord of Spirits.[a]

footnotes.text: The first denial concerns light that cannot be counted, followed by a denial of a limit measured in days. The darkness verb is from asking or examination, not another occurrence of passed away. The two following light-standing clauses are both retained.

source.text: በእማንቱ፡ መዋዕል፡ ርእያ፡ አዕይንትየ፡ ኅቡአተ፡ መባርቅት፡ ወ*ብርሃናት፡ ወኰነኔሆሙ፡ ወይበርቁ፡ ለበረከት፡ ወለመርገም፡ በከመ፡ ፈቂደ፡ እግዚአ፡ መንፈሳት።

translation.text: In those days my eyes saw the hidden things of the lightnings and lights, and their judgment. They flash for blessing and for curse, as the Lord of Spirits wills.[a]

footnotes.text: The selected text names both lightnings and lights, and their judgment. The paired purposes are blessing and curse; the curse is not softened or removed. These are the source’s images, not a modern physical explanation of lightning.

source.text: ወበህየ፡ ርኢኩ፡ *ኅቡአተ፡ ነጐድጓድ፡ ወከመ፡ ይደቅቅ፡ በመልዕልተ፡ ሰማይ፡ ወቃሎሙ፡ ይሰማዕ፡ †መማኅድረተ፡ የብስ፡ አስተርአየኒ፡ [ወቃለ፡ ዘነጐድጓድ፡] ለሰላም፡ ወለበረከት፡ ወእመ፡ ለመርገም፡ በቃለ፡ እግዚአ፡ መንፈሳት።
source.note: Actual Charles1906 complete-unit full-page and native400dpi visual collation. Printed stars, daggers, parentheses, square brackets and dots retained; raised apparatus references and verse labels excluded, punctuation spacing normalized. Printed editorial readings remain selected print, not independent manuscript certification. No reported variant outside this main-text base adopted. translation.text: There I saw the hidden things of thunder, how it crashes in the heights of heaven, and its voices are heard. He showed me dwelling places of dry land [and the voice of thunder], for peace and blessing, or for curse, by the word of the Lord of Spirits.[a]

footnotes.text: Not ready for publication: the selected dwelling-places expression is daggered and the following thunder-voice phrase is bracketed. Charles printed103 note23 discusses an underlying Greek corruption and proposes judgment-related alternatives, but this proposal adopts none. The provisional English retains dwellings and the bracketed voice instead of silently repairing the connection.

source.text: ወእምድኅረዝ፡ ተርእየ፡ ሊተ፡ ኵሎ፡ ኅቡአቲሆሙ፡ ለብርሃናት፡ ወለመባርቅት፡ ወለበረከት፡ ወለጽጋብ፡ ይበርቁ።
source.note: Actual Charles1906 complete-unit full-page and native400dpi visual collation. translation.text: After this all their hidden things were shown to me, those of the lights and lightnings: they flash for blessing and abundance.[a]

footnotes.text: The revelation is passive, shown to me. The closing flash is for blessing and abundance; abundance is not replaced with the curse from the preceding verse.

source.text: በዓመት፡ ኅምእት፡ በወርኅ፡ ሰብዕ፡ *አመ፡ ዐሥሩ፡ ወረቡዐ፡ ለወርኅ፡ በሕይወተ፡ ሄኖክ፡ በውእቱ፡ አምሳል፡ ርኢኩ፡ ከመ፡ ታደለቀልቅ፡ *ሰማየ፡ ሰማያት፡ *ድልቅልቅ፡ ዐቢይ፡ ወኀይለ፡ ልዑል፡ ወመላእክት፡ አእላፈ፡ አእላፍ፡ ወትእልፊተ፡ ትእልፊት፡ ተሀውኩ፡ *ሁከተ፡ ዐቢየ።
source.note: Actual Charles1906 complete-unit full-page and native400dpi visual collation. translation.text: In the five-hundredth year, in the seventh month, on the fourteenth day of the month, in the life of Enoch, I saw in that vision how the heaven of heavens shook with a great shaking. The host of the Most High and angels, myriads of myriads and ten-thousands of ten-thousands, were greatly troubled.[a]

footnotes.text: The selected date is the five-hundredth year, seventh month and fourteenth day, in Enoch’s life. Charles printed103 note39 discusses the name Enoch as an editorial replacement for Noah, but this proposal retains the actual selected name and does not adopt that conjecture. The multiplied myriad expressions are retained as large-number expressions, not converted into a modern population total.

source.text: ወርእሰ፡ መዋዕል፡ ዲበ፡ መንበረ፡ ስብሐቲሁ፡ ይነብር፡ ወመላእክት፡ ወጻድቃን፡ አውዶ፡ ይቀውሙ።
source.note: Actual Charles1906 complete-unit full-page and native400dpi visual collation. Printed stars, daggers, parentheses, square brackets and dots retained; raised apparatus references and verse labels excluded, punctuation spacing normalized. Printed editorial readings remain selected print, not independent manuscript certification. No reported variant outside this main-text base adopted. Independent exact-row review required.

translation.text: The Head of Days was sitting on the throne of his glory, and angels and righteous ones were standing around him.[a]

footnotes.text: This complete unit crosses onto the next page. The throne is the throne of his glory, and those standing around him include both angels and righteous ones. Head of Days is retained as a source title without inserting a later personal identification.

source.text: ወሊተ፡ ረዐድ፡ ዐቢይ፡ ነሥአኒ፡ ወፍርሃት፡ አኀዘኒ፡ ወሐቌየ፡ *ተቀጽዐ፡ ወ*ተፈትሐ፡ ኵለንትየ፡ ወወደቅኩ፡ በገጽየ።

translation.text: A great trembling took hold of me, and fear seized me. My loins were racked, my whole being came loose, and I fell on my face.[a]

footnotes.text: The source gives the narrator’s bodily collapse: trembling, fear, afflicted loins and loosening of his whole being, ending with falling on his face. The wording is not changed into an unprinted diagnosis or a calm bow.

source.text: ወፈነወ፡ ሚካኤል፡ ካልአ፡ መልአከ፡ እምቅዱሳን፡ ወአንሥአኒ፡ *ወሶበ፡ አንሥአኒ፡ መንፈስየ፡ ገብአት፡ እስመ፡ ኢክህልኩ፡ ተዐግሦ፡ ርእይ፡ ዝኩ፡ ኀይል፡ ወኪያሁ፡ ሁከት፡ ወአንቀልቀሎ፡ ሰማይ።
source.note: Actual Charles1906 complete-unit full-page and native400dpi visual collation. Printed stars, daggers, parentheses, square brackets and dots retained; raised apparatus references and verse labels excluded, punctuation spacing normalized. translation.text: Michael sent another angel from among the holy ones and raised me up. When he raised me, my spirit returned, for I could not bear the sight of that host, that tumult and shaking of heaven.[a]

footnotes.text: Michael is the named sender of another angel from among the holy ones. The following raising clause and returned spirit are retained, but the pronoun is not expanded into a new named agent. The narrator explicitly says he could not bear the sight.

source.text: ወይቤለኒ፡ ሚካኤል፡ ምንተ፡ ርእይ፡ ዘከመዝ፡ ተሀውከ፡ እስከ፡ ዮም፡ ሀለወት፡ ዕለተ፡ ምሕረት፡ ወሀሉ፡ መሐሪ፡ ወርኅቀ፡ መዐት፡ *ለእለ፡ እለ፡ ይኀድሩ፡ ዲበ፡ የብስ።

translation.text: Michael said to me, “What have you seen that has so troubled you? Until today the day of mercy has remained, and he has been merciful and slow to anger toward those who dwell on dry land.”[a]

footnotes.text: The selected statement describes mercy and slowness to anger toward those dwelling on dry land. The repeated relative construction is smoothed into English without changing the recipient group or adding a new date for judgment.

source.text: ወሶበ፡ ትመጽእ፡ *ዕለት፡ ወኀይል፡ ወመቅሠፍት፡ ወኰነኔ፡ እንተ፡ አስተዳለወ፡ እግዚአ፡ መንፈሳት፡ ለእለ፡ ኢይሰግዱ፡ ለኵነኔ፡ ጽድቅ፡ ወለእለ፡ *ይክሕዱ፡ ለኵነኔ፡ ጽድቅ፡ ወለእለ፡ ይነሥኡ፡ ስሞ፡ በከ፡ ወተደለወት፡ ይእቲ፡ ዕለት፡ ለኅሩያን፡ መሐላ፡ ወለኃጥአን፡ ሐተታ።....
source.note: Actual Charles1906 complete-unit full-page and native400dpi visual collation. translation.text: “When the day, the power, the punishment and the judgment come, which the Lord of Spirits has prepared for those who do not bow to righteous judgment, who deny righteous judgment and take his name in vain—that day has been prepared as an oath for the chosen and an inquiry for sinners…”[a]

footnotes.text: The selected source negates bowing to righteous judgment, includes denial of that judgment, and says taking his name in vain. The final selected nouns are oath for the chosen and inquiry for sinners; they are not replaced by a different promise. Four printed dots after the final sentence are represented by an ellipsis. Charles’s note on printed104 says verse25 should follow immediately, but this proposal keeps the printed unit order and does not invent a connecting conclusion.

source.text: ወተከፈሉ፡ *በይእቲ፡ ዕለት፡ ክልኤቱ፡ ዐናብርት፡ ዐንበር፡ አንስትያዊት፡ ዘስማ፡ ሌዋያታን፡ ከመ፡ ትኀድር፡ በልጐተ፡ ባሕር፡ መልዕልተ፡ አንቅዕተ፡ ማያት።

translation.text: On that day the two great beasts were separated: the female beast, whose name is Leviathan, to dwell in the depths of the sea above the springs of water.[a]

footnotes.text: The selected past-tense separation of two great beasts and the female designation of Leviathan are retained. The source says that day; it is not silently made a new prophecy in the future or a reference to the day of judgment. Depths of the sea follows the abyss/deep noun, not an identification with an ordinary animal species.

source.text: ወለተባዕታይ፡ ስሙ፡ ብሄሞት፡ ዘይኤኅዛ፡ በእንግድዓሁ፡ በደው፡ ዘኢያስተርኢ፡ ወስሙ፡ ዱንዳይን፡ በምሥራቀ፡ ገነት፡ በኀበ፡ ይነብሩ፡ *ኅሩያን፡ ወጻድቃን፡ በኀበ፡ ተመጠወ፡ እምኄውየ፡ ሰብዕ፡ እምአዳም፡ ቀዳሚሆሙ፡ ለሰብእ፡ ዘገብረ፡ እግዚአ፡ መንፈሳት።

translation.text: The male is named Behemoth. With his breast he takes possession of an unseen wilderness, whose name is Dundayin, east of the garden where the chosen and righteous dwell, where my forefather was received, the seventh from Adam, the first of the people whom the Lord of Spirits made.[a]

footnotes.text: Not ready for publication: the proper-name spelling provisionally represented as Dundayin and the beast’s taking-possession with its breast remain uncertain in this author proposal. For the treasury of their number is of sand, and each of them is held with a bridle and turns by the force of the wind, and is driven in this way according to the skill surrounding the earth.[a]

translation.text: The wind of dew has its dwelling at the ends of heaven and adjoins the storehouses of rain. Its course is in winter and summer. The rain cloud and the cloud of mist join together, and one gives to the other.[a]

footnotes.text: The selected text locates dew’s dwelling at heaven’s ends and pairs it with rain’s storehouses. The rain and mist clouds join and give to one another. Winter and summer are retained without adding a regional meteorological calendar.

footnotes.text: The source explains rain as nourishment from the Most High in heaven for those dwelling on dry land and gives rain a measure. The angels receive it; the selected verb is not silently changed to the opposite direction of transfer.

source.text: ለእሉ፡ ኵሎሙ፡ ርኢኩ፡ እስከ፡ ገነተ፡ ጻድቃን።

translation.text: I saw all these things as far as the garden of the righteous.[a]

footnotes.text: The selected boundary is as far as the garden of the righteous. This single unit contains no added description of that garden or a new journey into it.

translation.text: The angel of peace who was walking with me said to me, “These two great beasts were prepared by the hand of God; he will provide food… [so that the punishment of the Lord of Spirits, when it kills children with their mothers and children with their fathers].”[a]

footnotes.text: Not ready for publication: six printed dots follow the providing-food verb, and the following punishment clause is square-bracketed. Charles printed108 note22 identifies the bracketed passage as a repetition from verse25 with a missing word. This proposal keeps the bracketed text visible in the source and provisional English; it does not silently delete it, supply a recipient of food, or borrow a verb from a later English translation.

source.text: ሶበ፡ ተኀርፍ፡ መቅሠፍት፡ ለእግዚአ፡ መንፈሳት፡ ዲቤሆሙ፡ ታኀርፍ፡ ከመ፡ ኢትምጻእ፡ መቅሠፍት፡ ለእግዚአ፡ መንፈሳት፡ በከ፡ ወትቀትል፡ ደቂቀ፡ ምስለ፡ እማቲሆሙ፡ ወደቂቀ፡ ምስለ፡ አበዊሆሙ፡ [ሶበ፡ ተኀርፍ፡ መቅሠፍት፡ ለእግዚአ፡ መንፈሳት፡ ዲበ፡ እሉ፡] ድኅረ፡ ትከውን፡ ኵነኔ፡ በምሕረት፡ ወበትዕግሥት።

translation.text: When the punishment of the Lord of Spirits rests upon them, it will rest so that the punishment of the Lord of Spirits does not come in vain. It will kill children with their mothers and children with their fathers. [When the punishment of the Lord of Spirits rests upon these,] afterward judgment will be in mercy and patience.[a]

footnotes.text: The printed square-bracketed when-punishment-rests clause is retained in English as a bracketed repetition. Charles printed108 note31 treats it as a possible repetition but also discusses whether it could introduce the following clause. No unbracketed reconstruction is adopted. The text explicitly includes children with mothers and children with fathers, the not-in-vain denial, and mercy and patience in the final judgment statement.

translation.text: In those days I saw that long cords were given to those angels. They took wings for themselves, flew, and went toward the north.[a]

footnotes.text: The selected text has long cords, wings, flying, and a journey northward. It does not say how many angels there were. The passive giving and their taking wings are retained without introducing an unprinted named giver.

translation.text: I asked the angel, “Why have these taken cords and gone?” He said to me, “They have gone to measure.”[a]

footnotes.text: The question and answer continue across the page. The question is why the cords were taken, and the answer is that they went to measure. No measurement result is supplied in this unit.

translation.text: The angel who was walking with me said to me, “These will bring the measures of the righteous and the bonds of the righteous to the righteous, so that they may lean upon the name of the Lord of Spirits for ever and ever.”[a]

footnotes.text: Both the measures and bonds of the righteous are selected nouns; bonds is not silently omitted. The ending is leaning upon the name of the Lord of Spirits for ever and ever, preserving the explicit name and title.

source.text: ይመጥኑ፡ ወይኀድሩ፡ ኅሩያን፡ ምስለ፡ ኅሩያን፡ ወእሉ፡ አምጣናት፡ እለ፡ ይትወሀቡ፡ ለኀይማኖት፡ *ወያጸንዕዋ፡ ለጽድቅ።

translation.text: “They will measure, and the chosen will dwell with the chosen. These measures will be given for faith, and they will strengthen righteousness.”[a]

footnotes.text: Not ready for publication: the selected first clause has measuring and chosen dwelling with chosen. The relations of subjects, the following measures-for-faith clause and the righteousness object remain provisional. The draft does not silently replace dwelling with judging or make the measures an imported restoration of a building.

translation.text: “These measures will reveal all the hidden things in the depth of the earth: those who perished in the wilderness, those devoured by wild beasts and those devoured by the fish of the sea, so that they may return and find support on the day of the chosen one. Nothing perishes before the Lord of Spirits, and nothing can perish.”[a]

footnotes.text: The lost people in wilderness, those eaten by wild beasts and those eaten by sea fish are all retained. Return and leaning are distinct verbs. Both final denials of perishing remain; the source is not changed into a claim that the listed deaths never occurred.

translation.text: All those in the height of heaven received a command, and power, a voice and a light like fire.[a]

translation.text: The Lord of Spirits seated the chosen one upon the throne of glory. He will judge all the works of the holy ones in the height of heaven, and their works will be weighed in the balance.[a]

footnotes.text: The Lord of Spirits seats the chosen one; the next judging action belongs to that enthroned figure. The selected objects explicitly include works of the holy ones, not a silent replacement with sinners. Weighing in the balance remains the text’s judgment image.

translation.text: When he raises his face to judge their ways, those of the chosen, by the word of the name of the Lord of Spirits, and their tracks in the way of righteous judgment of the Lord of Spirits, all of them will speak with a voice and bless, praise, exalt and sanctify the name of the Lord of Spirits.[a]

The draft does not add an unprinted one-voice numeral here, a new judging agent, or a repaired Greek clause. The following blessing, praise, exaltation and sanctification sequence is complete.

translation.text: On that day they will take up one voice and bless, praise and exalt in the spirit of faith, the spirit of wisdom, the spirit of patience, the spirit of mercy, the spirit of judgment and peace, and the spirit of goodness. All of them will say with one voice, “Blessed be the name of the Lord of Spirits, and may it be blessed for ever and ever.”[a]

footnotes.text: The selected source explicitly has one voice twice. Faith, wisdom, patience, mercy, judgment and peace, and goodness are retained in order. The blessed-name formula and everlasting conclusion are not clipped.

translation.text: All who do not sleep in the height of heaven will bless him. All the holy ones in heaven will bless him, and all the chosen who dwell in the garden of life. Every spirit of light that can bless, praise, exalt and sanctify your blessed name, and all flesh, beyond its strength, will praise and bless your name for ever and ever.[a]

footnotes.text: The source distinguishes those who do not sleep, the holy ones, the chosen in the garden of life and every spirit of light. The relative light-spirit phrase is a capacity expression, can, not a new negative. The bracketed relative before beyond-its-strength is kept in the source. The shift from him to your blessed name is retained rather than normalized throughout to third person.

source.text: እስመ፡ ብዝኀ፡ ምሕረቱ፡ ለእግዚአ፡ መንፈሳት፡ ወርኁቀ፡ መዐት፡ *ወኵሎ፡ ግብረ፡ ወኵሎ፡ አምጣነ፡ ገብረ፡ ከሠተ፡ *ለጻድቃን፡ ወለኅሩያን፡ *በስመ፡ ለእግዚአ፡ መንፈሳት።

translation.text: For the Lord of Spirits is rich in mercy and slow to anger. All the work and every measure that he has made he revealed to the righteous and the chosen, in the name of the Lord of Spirits.[a]

footnotes.text: The selected text says rich in mercy and slow to anger, then all work and every measure he made. The revelation is to the righteous and the chosen. No fresh personal identification or unprinted scope of creation is inserted.
